definition: AI in education technology — tutoring systems, adaptive learning, and automated assessment.
details: AI in education technology — tutoring systems, adaptive learning, and automated assessment.

explainer.lead: AI in education technology uses software to support tutoring, adjust learning activities, and assess work automatically. It matters because these tools can respond to an individual learner rather than giving everyone exactly the same sequence.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a study helper that notices which questions you find hard. It can give you a hint, choose a little more practice, and check your answers before moving you on.
tiers.practitioner: Applications combine learner responses with tutoring, content-selection, or automated-assessment components, often within an online learning platform. A practical pitfall is treating an automatically chosen activity or score as reliable without checking it against learner outcomes.
tiers.paperLevel: Let s_t represent estimates of a learner's state at time t; an adaptive policy selects activity a_t, and subsequent responses update the state. AI + edtech is an application area rather than a single algorithm, so its behavior and limits depend on the tutoring, adaptation, and assessment methods used.

explainer.example: A student misses several algebra questions involving fractions. The system provides a worked hint, assigns easier fraction practice, automatically checks the answers, and then offers another algebra question.

usedIn.name: Intelligent tutoring
usedIn.detail: Providing guidance and feedback while a learner works through a task.

usedIn.name: Adaptive learning
usedIn.detail: Selecting activities according to a learner's responses and progress.

usedIn.name: Automated assessment
usedIn.detail: Using software to evaluate submitted answers or work.

explainer.intuition: Instead of treating every learner identically, the software uses responses to decide what help, practice, or evaluation to provide next.
howItWorks: Collect a learner's answers or other work.
Estimate what the learner appears to understand or find difficult.
Select tutoring, feedback, or further practice.
Assess new responses and update the next step.
explainer.whyItMatters: It connects instruction, practice, and assessment in a repeatable loop that can be adjusted to an individual learner.
misconceptions: It is not one algorithm or product; it covers several educational uses of AI.
Automated assessment is only one part, alongside tutoring and adaptive learning.

diagram.caption: Assessment and learner responses feed a loop that selects tutoring and practice.
